stories.title: NBA China Games — Mavericks vs. Rockets, Game 1 Tonight in Macao

x_posts.label: Post 1
x_posts.text:
Cooper Flagg tips off his first global NBA stage TONIGHT.

Mavericks vs. Rockets | The Venetian Arena, Macao 🌏
7:30 PM CST — Game 1 of the NBA China Games 2026.

The world is watching No. 1. #Mavericks

x_posts.label: Post 2
x_posts.text:
Kevin Durant. Alperen Sengun. Amen Thompson.

Houston is bringing HEAT to Macao tonight.

Rockets vs. Mavericks in the NBA China Games — this is the matchup the league wanted on the world stage. #Rockets

facebook.long_form:
The NBA's biggest global event of the preseason tips off TONIGHT — and it couldn't have a better headliner.

Cooper Flagg. The No. 1 pick in the 2025 NBA Draft. Nineteen years old. Carrying a Dallas Mavericks franchise on his shoulders and taking it to the world stage for the first time.

Tonight at 7:30 PM CST, the Mavericks tip off against the Houston Rockets at The Venetian Arena in Macao, China — Game 1 of the NBA China Games 2026. Game 2 follows on October 11.

For the Mavericks, this is Cooper Flagg's first international preseason appearance. Alongside Kyrie Irving, Flagg gets his first real look at what it means to be a global NBA ambassador. For the Rockets, Kevin Durant, Alperen Sengun and Amen Thompson give the league another marquee name to sell to Asian audiences.

This is the 16th edition of the NBA China Games. Tickets sold through Cotai Ticketing, Taobao 88VIP, Trip.com and MPay. The games will be broadcast in 200+ countries and territories.

One question heading into tonight: How does Cooper Flagg handle his first game in front of a non-American NBA crowd? The spotlight has followed him his entire career. This is a new kind of test.

What time will you be watching?
facebook.image_caption: Cooper Flagg takes the NBA global. Game 1 of the China Games tips off TONIGHT in Macao. #Mavericks #NBAChina

article.headline: Cooper Flagg Steps Onto the World Stage: NBA China Games 2026 Preview

stories.title: Sixers Lose Backup Center Hukporti to Torn Achilles — Season Over

x_posts.label: Post 3
x_posts.text:
BREAKING: Ariel Hukporti has torn his right Achilles tendon.

The 76ers backup center is out for the entire 2026-27 season.

Philly is $1.8M under the first apron with almost no room to replace him. #Sixers

x_posts.label: Post 4
x_posts.text:
Hukporti tore his LEFT Achilles in 2022. Now his right.

24 years old. Two Achilles tears. Coming off winning a title with the Knicks last year.

Some stories are just brutal. Heal up, Ariel. 💙 #Sixers

facebook.long_form:
The Philadelphia 76ers entered this preseason with the most star-studded roster in the Eastern Conference. LeBron James. Joel Embiid. Jaylen Brown. Tyrese Maxey.

And in a single non-contact play in their first preseason game, the entire enterprise got more fragile.

Ariel Hukporti — the 24-year-old center the Sixers signed in July to be Embiid's primary backup — ruptured his right Achilles tendon in the first quarter against the Knicks on October 5. An MRI confirmed the diagnosis. Surgery was performed successfully on October 6. His season is over.

What makes this particularly troubling for Philadelphia: the Sixers are only $1.8 million under the first apron. That cap position severely limits their ability to sign a replacement without waiving a player or making a small trade.

For now, Adem Bona steps in as the primary backup behind Embiid. Bona is a capable defender, but Hukporti's combination of size, mobility and championship pedigree (he won a title with the Knicks last season) is hard to replicate cheaply.

And if that weren't enough, this is the second major Achilles injury of Hukporti's career. He tore his LEFT Achilles in 2022 while playing for Melbourne United in Australia's NBL.

Nobody wants to see a young player go through this twice. The Sixers will find a way forward — they're still the favorites in the East — but this is a story that deserved more than a footnote.
facebook.image_caption: Prayers for Ariel Hukporti. The 76ers center is out for the season with a torn Achilles — his second in four years. #Sixers

article.headline: Hukporti's Torn Achilles Exposes the Sixers' Hidden Vulnerability

stories.title: Pelicans Overcome 24-Point Deficit to Beat Thunder 116-110

x_posts.label: Post 5
x_posts.text:
New Orleans was down 24 points.

They won anyway.

Pelicans 116, Thunder 110 — Jamahl Mosley gets his first win as head coach in the most dramatic way possible. Mathurin: 13 PTS off the bench. 🔥 #Pelicans

facebook.long_form:
Down 24 points. In a new coach's first game. On a neutral court.

The New Orleans Pelicans just gave Jamahl Mosley the most emphatic possible introduction to the NBA head coaching ranks.

New Orleans trailed by 24 in the first half against Oklahoma City at the BOK Center in Tulsa on Wednesday. The Thunder — without Shai Gilgeous-Alexander and most of their starters — were supposed to be the perfect opponent to build early confidence. Instead, they jumped out to a massive lead and the Pelicans had to earn every inch of the comeback.

They did. New Orleans outscored OKC 38-26 in the third quarter, slicing the deficit to three points heading into the final period. Then they pulled it out, outscoring the Thunder 26-17 in the fourth to win 116-110.

Bennedict Mathurin led the Pelicans with 13 points off the bench. Bennett Stirtz paced OKC with 15 points, 6 assists and 5 rebounds.

Was this the most important game of the preseason? No. But in sports, momentum and belief matter — and this team just chose both, loudly.

Welcome to the NBA, Coach Mosley.
facebook.image_caption: Down 24. Still won. The Pelicans are built different in 2026-27. 🔥 #Pelicans

article.headline: Down 24, Still Won: Pelicans Give Jamahl Mosley the Perfect Welcome

stories.title: Giannis and the Heat — Debut Done, Eyes on October 21

x_posts.label: Post 6
x_posts.text:
Giannis Antetokounmpo's Heat debut: 9 PTS | 7 AST | 3-3 FG | 14 MIN.

Miami won 129-105. The Bucks legend looked right at home in Miami's system.

Regular season opener vs. the Timberwolves: October 21. 🔥 #HeatNation

facebook.long_form:
On October 3, in a historic first: the NBA held a preseason game in Quebec City, Canada. And the player who made the evening unforgettable was Giannis Antetokounmpo, making his very first appearance in a Miami Heat uniform.

The result: Miami 129, Toronto 105. The stat line: 9 points, 7 assists (game-high), 3-of-3 from the field, 14 minutes.

For a first game in a new system under a new coach after 13 seasons with the Milwaukee Bucks, that's exactly what you want to see. No forced shots. High assist numbers. Efficient offense. Giannis let the game come to him — a sign that he's genuinely bought into Erik Spoelstra's system.

But the debut is done. Now comes the real work.

The Heat have a loaded preseason schedule remaining:
- Oct. 8: vs. New Orleans Pelicans (last night — result TBD)
- Oct. 10: vs. Minnesota Timberwolves
- Oct. 14: vs. Brooklyn Nets
- Oct. 16: at Orlando Magic

Then the regular season begins. And on October 21 at Kaseya Center, Giannis faces the Minnesota Timberwolves in the Heat's regular-season opener — which will also mark his first home regular-season game in Miami.

Klay Thompson. Bobby Portis. Tim Hardaway Jr. This Heat roster was built to win now, and all the pieces are being assembled around the two-time MVP. The preseason is the audition. Opening Night is the show.
facebook.image_caption: Smooth debut. Now the real work begins. Giannis and the Heat: Oct. 21 is the date to circle. 🌊 #HeatNation

article.headline: Giannis Checked Every Box in His Heat Debut — Now the Real Work Begins

stories.title: Stephen Curry Signs 2-Year, $116M Extension — Stays a Warrior for Life

x_posts.label: Post 7
x_posts.text:
Stephen Curry just turned down an extra $20M+ to stay a Warrior.

2 years. $116M. Player option in year 2.

He could have had $136.7M. He chose loyalty.

That's Steph. ☘️ #Warriors

facebook.long_form:
Stephen Curry has never played for any team other than the Golden State Warriors. In a league defined by player movement, free agency chaos and superteam-building, that's a remarkable statement of loyalty.

Now he's extended it further.

Curry agreed to a 2-year, $116M contract extension with Golden State, running through the 2028-29 season with a player option in the final year. By the time the deal expires, Curry will have spent roughly 20 seasons as a Warrior.

Here's the part worth noting: he didn't have to take that deal. Curry was eligible for up to $136.7M over two years. He discounted himself by more than $20M — a significant amount at any level, and a choice that few players of his stature would make.

Why the discount? According to ESPN, Curry ultimately chose security and the continuation of his legacy over maximizing his earning potential. He believes in the Golden State organization. He wants to finish his career there.

And yet, this is still a massive commitment. $116M is life-altering money by any measure, and the Warriors are betting that Curry can continue performing at an elite level into his late 30s. Based on the preseason — where he scored 16 points in under 15 minutes against the Lakers — there's no reason to doubt that.

Steph Curry, Warrior for life. Some things in the NBA remain sacred.
facebook.image_caption: Steph passed on $20M to stay a Warrior. Loyalty still exists in the NBA. 🏆 #Warriors

article.headline: Curry Takes a Discount to Stay a Warrior: Inside the 2-Year, $116M Extension
